desc:
The array nums is sorted in non-decreasing order. Remove the duplicates so that every distinct value appears exactly once, keeping the values in order. Return the resulting array.

Aim for O(n) time and O(1) extra space by overwriting the array in place.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order
hints: Equal values are adjacent because the array is sorted, so a duplicate is just an element equal to its predecessor.
Keep a slow pointer at the end of the deduplicated prefix and a fast pointer that scans ahead.
When nums[fast] differs from nums[slow], advance slow and copy the value there. The answer is the first slow + 1 elements.
editorial: Since equal values are grouped together, each new distinct value is the first element after a run of equal ones. Let slow point at the last value kept. For each fast from 1 onward, if nums[fast] != nums[slow] then it is a new value: increment slow and write nums[fast] into that slot.

At the end the first slow + 1 positions hold the distinct values in order. The array is scanned once, so time is O(n); only two indices are used, so space is O(1) beyond the returned slice. Remember to handle the empty array.
